issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the example usage in Main expect Meal constructor with signature Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template's Meal class defines the constructor with parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This mismatch will cause compile errors for students using the provided example and conflicts with the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update the parameter assignment order accordingly so it matches the UML, the example usage in Main, and the solution implementation.

issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent: the problem statement and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (UML and example usage in Main), but the template defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch prevents a direct mapping from the problem description and example code to the template, will confuse students about the intended constructor signature, and can cause compilation/usage errors when following the provided examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the problem statement and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (swap the parameter order) so that example usages (e.g., new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})) and the UML specification align with the template implementation.
